page: Microsoft Azure D32ps_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the Dpsv6 server family. It is powered by a Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processor with an arm64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz. The instance features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs, meaning there is no hyperthreading. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 128 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include any local storage or bundled GPUs, though it is Premium Storage capable.

In benchmark evaluations, the D32ps_v6 demonstrates strong multi-core performance and exceptional memory throughput. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench multi-core scores are rated as strong, reflecting the efficiency of its 32 dedicated ARM cores. Memory bandwidth tests show top-tier performance for both large-block read-only and large-block write operations, alongside a top-tier Passmark memory score. Database operations also rank in the top tier, with Passmark database operations scoring high and Redis SET operations achieving strong throughput. Single-core performance across stress-ng and Geekbench remains in the average tier.

Given its balanced resource profile and high memory bandwidth, the D32ps_v6 is highly cost-efficient for scale-out workloads that benefit from dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading. It is well-suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, static web serving, and database operations. However, due to the lack of local storage and GPU accelerators, it is less suitable for heavy local storage-bound databases or large-scale LLM inference, where prompt processing for large models falls into the poor performance tier.
